title: Parking Lot Implementation
description: A code walkthrough implementing the parking lot design in Java and Python, covering classes, methods, and key data structures.

segments.text: We designed the parking lot on paper. Now let's bring it to life with code. I will walk you through implementations in both Java and Python so you can see the patterns in action.

Start with VehicleType as an enum: CAR, BIKE, TRUCK. Then an abstract Vehicle class with licensePlate and vehicleType. Each subclass like Car simply sets its type in the constructor. Clean, extensible.
ParkingSpot has spotId, size, isOccupied, and a vehicle reference. The canFitVehicle method compares the vehicle size to the spot size. The park and unpark methods update the state atomically.
The Floor class holds a list of ParkingSpots. Its findAvailableSpot method iterates through spots, checking canFitVehicle. In Java, use a HashMap grouping spots by size for O(1) lookup by type.

segments.thought_prompt: Should findAvailableSpot return the first available spot or the best available spot? What criteria define 'best'?

segments.text: ParkingLot is the facade. It holds a list of Floors and a ticketMap. The entry method finds a spot across all floors, creates a Ticket, and returns it. The exit method calculates the fee and releases the spot.
Ticket stores ticketId, entryTime, vehicle, assignedSpot, and paymentStatus. In Python, use dataclasses for clean syntax. In Java, use a record or builder pattern for immutable ticket creation.

Payment calculation uses the Strategy pattern. HourlyPricing and FlatRatePricing both implement a PricingStrategy interface. The parking lot injects the strategy at construction. Swap pricing models without changing core logic.

In a real system, multiple cars enter simultaneously. In Java, synchronize the entry method or use ReentrantLock on each spot. In Python, use threading.Lock. The critical section is: check availability, then park. These two steps must be atomic.

A DisplayBoard observes the parking lot using the Observer pattern. When a spot changes state, the board updates its available count per floor. In Java, use PropertyChangeListener. In Python, a simple callback list works.

segments.thought_prompt: How would you unit test the ParkingLot class? What edge cases would you cover?

segments.text: Test full lot, wrong vehicle size, duplicate exit, concurrent entry. The code walkthrough shows how design patterns translate to real implementations. Strategy for pricing, Observer for displays, Facade for the entry point. These are patterns you will use every day.
